next_question: Can a production-like testbed server be redesigned with a structural signal definition that is provably independent of behavioral state — specifically, header-only structural signal (ETag variation, Cache-Control variation, dynamic timestamp/request_id entropy) that excludes error response bodies entirely — and does orthogonality hold at delta=0.15 under this corrected measurement?
why_next: This experiment (EXP-GRAPH-35445595108) tested C-FRESHNESS orthogonality on a production-like local testbed server with CDN simulation, OAuth2 middleware, and dynamic content. The testbed infrastructure is sound and functional (304 rate 31.67%, behavioral TP 1.0, genuine ETag/Cache-Control/PyJWT RS256). However, the measurement is invalid: the structural signal definition (hash(body)%10000) includes 401 error response bodies, which are constant when tokens expire (audit V1_CRITICAL_SHARED_VARIABLE_CONFOUND). This creates a forced correlation (r=0.375) that is an artifact of the signal definition, not evidence that CDN/OAuth/dynamic content breaks orthogonality. The testbed can be reused with corrected signal extraction. Key fix: define structural signal from headers-only or success-body-only, excluding error response bodies. B-FLASK-ONLY baseline must also be included to discriminate infrastructure-induced vs definition-induced correlation.
